refuted.claim: Fact 8 (marked 'likely'): "The 'L = 1 or 6' on the One Field timing formulas is not a second decode variant ... The L=1 entry documents the timing of that chained continuation, not a distinct instruction decode."
refuted.why: The conclusion (one execution path, no decode-time variant) is correct, but the stated reason is wrong: the One-Field timing formula cannot be the timing of a chained arithmetic op. A22-0526-3 p.17 prints the One-Field formula as T = 4.5(L + 1 + A + 1.5A) with NO E term, while Figure 7 (p.12) defines E as "1 on a single-character add, subtract, zero and add, zero and subtract, table lookup". The Two-Fields formula T = 4.5(L + 1 + E + A + 1.5B + 1.5RB) explicitly carries "When L = 1, E = 1". At L=6 the two formulas agree exactly (E=0, R=0); at L=1 they disagree by one cycle. The hardware settles it: 223-2589 p.52 'Arithmetic Op Codes' and the CE Handbook ALD objective "Arithmetic-Type Op Codes ... SET D CYCLE CONTROL at I 1 or 1401 and I 3, with B channel WM" say a chained arithmetic op DOES take an extra D cycle, i.e. E=1.
refuted.correction: The 'or 1' on the One-Field 'L = 1 or 6' line is editorial carryover and its formula is one cycle short for L=1. The authoritative timing for a 1-character chained A/S/ZA/ZS is the TWO-FIELDS formula with L=1, E=1. Same edition-to-edition: A22-1407-2 (Nov61) prints the identical 'L = 1 or 6' lines, so this is not an OCR or a -3-edition artifact. Emulator consequence: only if you model cycle timing; the execution semantics conclusion is unaffected.
refuted.source: IBM A22-0526-3 1410 Principles of Operation, Figure 7 p.12 and pp.17-19 (http://bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/A22-0526-3_1410_princOps.pdf); IBM A22-1407-2 1410 Reference Manual Nov61 (http://bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/A22-1407-2_1410ref_Nov61.pdf); IBM 223-2589 1410 System Fundamentals p.52 (http://bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/223-2589_Instruction_Reference_1410_System_Fundamentals_Nov63.pdf)

refuted.claim: Table 1, L=1 column for Multiply (@) and Divide (%): "AAR, BAR unchanged; C cycle updates CAR. Two-field" — i.e. a chained multiply/divide takes only a C cycle.
refuted.why: 223-2589 p.52 'Chaining Circuit Description' is a single numbered sequence: steps 6-10 initiate and complete the D cycle ("Set D Cycle Ctrl — I1, B Ch WM, I Cycle, Arith Type Op Codes"; multiply and divide ARE arithmetic-type per the same page's grouping), and step 11 then adds "When the op code is multiply or divide, a C cycle must be taken to update the CAR." A22-0526-3 Figure 7 corroborates arithmetically: E = 2 on a single-character multiply or divide versus E = 1 on a single-character add/subtract/ZA/ZS — two extra cycles, not one.
refuted.correction: A chained (1-character) multiply or divide takes a D cycle (BAR -> STAR -> DAR) AND THEN a C cycle (to update CAR). That is why E=2. AAR and BAR are still untouched, so the two-field conclusion stands.
refuted.source: IBM 223-2589 1410 System Fundamentals p.52, 'Arithmetic Op Codes' + 'Chaining Circuit Description' steps 6-11 (http://bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/223-2589_Instruction_Reference_1410_System_Fundamentals_Nov63.pdf); A22-0526-3 Figure 7 p.12

refuted.claim: Implementer's rule and Table 1, L=6 column: "NOT address-double: AAR <- A only, BAR chained from previous E phase" for Multiply/Divide, and "L=11: AAR <- A-address, BAR <- B-address (add-type also copies into CAR/DAR)".
refuted.why: Both mis-state CAR/DAR. 223-2589 p.52: "Rd 1st Addr to AAR and CAR — B Ch WM, Not % Type Op codes" — the A address goes into CAR for EVERY not-percent-type op code, not only add-type. "The A field of not address double-type op codes is read into the AAR'S and CAR'S only." And for the B address: "The B field address is read into the BAR and DAR in the same way the A-field address is read in" — so after any 11-character two-address instruction DAR holds the B address, address-double or not. A 6-character multiply/divide additionally takes a D cycle at I ring 6 to rebuild DAR from the chained BAR: CE Handbook, 'Multiply or Divide Op Codes (13.14.01)' — "SET D CYCLE CONTROL at I 6 or 1401 and I 8 with B ch WM" and "LAST INSTRUCTION READ OUT CYCLE CONDITION at I 6 or 1401 and I 8 with D cycle". Add-type is the opposite: 'Add-Type Op Codes (13.14.02)' — "Sets NO D CYCLE AT I RING 6 OPS" (because DAR was already loaded with the doubled address).
refuted.correction: L=6 Multiply/Divide: AAR <- A, CAR <- A, BAR unchanged (chained), then a D cycle sets DAR <- BAR. E=1. L=6 A/S/ZA/ZS: AAR=BAR=CAR=DAR <- A, no D cycle, E=0. L=11 any two-address op: AAR<-A, CAR<-A, BAR<-B, DAR<-B, no D cycle, E=0.
refuted.source: IBM 223-2589 1410 System Fundamentals p.52 (http://bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/223-2589_Instruction_Reference_1410_System_Fundamentals_Nov63.pdf); IBM 223-2588-2 1410 CE Handbook, Common Op Code Grouping Line Objectives, 'Multiply or Divide Op Codes (13.14.01)' and 'Add-Type Op Codes (13.14.02)' (https://bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/CE_Instruction_Reference_Maintenance/223-2588-2_1410_CE_Handbook_196404.pdf)

refuted.claim: Fact 5: "Compare-Type op codes are explicitly 'NOT ADDRESS DOUBLE TYPE OP CODES'."
refuted.why: The ALD objective text reads "NOT ADDRESS DOUBLE TYPE OP CODES if not 1401". The finding drops the qualifier. The same qualifier appears on the add-type line the finding DID quote in full ("Sets ADDRESS DOUBLE TYPE OP CODES if not 1401"), on Multiply-or-Divide ("NOT ADDRESS DOUBLE OP CODES if not 1401"), on Two-Characters-Only, and on Word Mark Op Codes ("ADDRESS DOUBLE OP CODES if not 1401"). Dropping it matters precisely because the finding's own open question #4 is about 1401 mode.
refuted.correction: Every address-double grouping line in the 1410 ALDs is gated on 'if not 1401'. In 1401 compatibility mode the 1410's address-double op-code group is not driven at all; doubling in 1401 mode comes from the 1401 I-cycle logic instead (see the addition on A24-1403-5).
refuted.source: IBM 223-2588-2 1410 CE Handbook, Common Op Code Grouping Line Objectives, 'Compare-Type Op Codes (13.14.03)' (https://bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/CE_Instruction_Reference_Maintenance/223-2588-2_1410_CE_Handbook_196404.pdf)

refuted.claim: Fact 7: "A22-0526-3 documents Add/Subtract/ZA/ZS as two separate 'Instruction Form' entries, Two Fields (L = 1 or 11) and One Field (L = 1 or 6)" ... citing "pp.17-18".
refuted.why: Two errors. (a) The Two-Fields entries print no 'L =' line at all. Only the One-Field entries carry an explicit 'L = 1 or 6.' line; the Two-Fields entries carry only the timing note "When L = 1, E = 1; when L = 11, E = 0." from which L in {1,11} is an inference. Presenting '(L = 1 or 11)' as a documented Instruction Form field is not what the page says. (b) The eight entries span pp.17-19, not pp.17-18: Zero and Subtract (One Field) is on page 19 (A22-0526-3 index: "ZERO AND SUBTRACT ( ONE FIELD ) page 19"). Table 2's row for that instruction likewise lists page 18 and should be 19.
refuted.correction: Add (Two Fields) p.17, Add (One Field) p.17, Subtract (Two Fields) p.17, Subtract (One Field) p.18, Zero and Add (Two Fields) p.18, Zero and Add (One Field) p.18, Zero and Subtract (Two Fields) p.18, Zero and Subtract (One Field) p.19. Valid lengths for the Two-Fields forms are derived from the E note, not printed as an L list.
refuted.source: IBM A22-0526-3 1410 Principles of Operation, pp.17-19 and the manual's own alphabetic instruction index (http://bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/A22-0526-3_1410_princOps.pdf)

refuted.claim: Fact 14 cites 223-2589 "p.51" for "Not Percent-Type Op Codes: Only these op codes (except R and X) can be chained."
refuted.why: That sentence opens the 'COMMON OP-CODE GROUPING LINES' section, which follows the full-page '1410 OP CODES' grouping chart on p.49 and sits between the p.48 and p.50 folios in the scan. p.51 ends with the running foot '1411 Functional Units 51'; the 'Address Double-Type Op Codes' / 'Chaining' text the finding also cites begins after that foot and is correctly on p.52.
refuted.correction: The 'Not Percent-Type Op Codes ... (except R and X) can be chained' sentence is on 223-2589 p.50. The address-double / chaining / arithmetic-op-code text is on p.52 (that citation was right). Also worth carrying into the claim text itself: R and X — the overlapped-I/O branch op codes — are not-percent-type yet still cannot be chained, so 'not percent-type' is necessary but not sufficient.

refuted.claim: Fact 10 body: "unlike A, S, ZA, ZS, C(S), B, ZS and CWM which carry O_DBL" in rcornwell/sims op_args[64].
refuted.why: The list duplicates ZS and is incomplete. Reading I7000/i7010_cpu.c op_args[64] directly, the entries carrying O_DBL are: 021 CS (O_AB|O_DBL), 022 S, 027 IO2 (O_A|O_M|O_DBL), 033 SWM, 041 B (O_A|O_M|O_DBL), 051 IO1 (O_A|O_M|O_DBL), 052 ZS, 061 A, 072 ZA, 074 CWM. The finding omits SWM, IO1 and IO2.
refuted.correction: 1410-mode O_DBL set in i7010_cpu.c = { CS, S, IO2, SWM, B, IO1, ZS, A, ZA, CWM }. Multiply (014), Divide (034), Compare (063), T (023), MOV (064), BCE (062), BBE (026) carry no O_DBL — that part of the finding is correct.

refuted.claim: Sources note on 223-2589: "The only 1410 PDF with a real text layer."
refuted.why: False. A22-0526-3 (1410 Principles of Operation), A22-1407-2 (1410 Reference Manual Nov61) and 223-2588-2 (1410 CE Handbook) all yield usable text via pdftotext -layout; every A22-0526-3 and CE Handbook quotation in this verification pass was extracted that way.
refuted.correction: Drop the claim. The practical caveat is different and more useful: the OCR text layer of the two-column 'Common Op Code Grouping Chart' (223-2589 p.49; CE Handbook) is column-misaligned and cannot be parsed row-to-op-code reliably — a per-row shift fit fails to reproduce even known rows (it renders 'Arith Type Op Codes' as 4 ops instead of the documented 6). Use the prose and the ALD grouping-line objectives instead of that chart.

upgraded.claim: Fact 10 (was 'likely'): A 6-character Multiply or Divide on the 1410 loads AAR (and CAR) and chains the B address from the previous operation, because @ and % are not address-double-type op codes.
upgraded.source: Now verified in two primary sources plus the oracle. (1) IBM 223-2588-2 1410 CE Handbook, 'Multiply or Divide Op Codes (13.14.01)': "NOT ADDRESS DOUBLE OP CODES if not 1401 ... SET D CYCLE CONTROL at I 6 or 1401 and I 8 with B ch WM" (https://bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/CE_Instruction_Reference_Maintenance/223-2588-2_1410_CE_Handbook_196404.pdf). (2) IBM 223-2589 p.52: "The A field of not address double-type op codes is read into the AAR'S and CAR'S only" and "Not address double-type op codes use the contents remaining in the BAR at the completion of the previous E phase for the B field address" (http://bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/223-2589_Instruction_Reference_1410_System_Fundamentals_Nov63.pdf). (3) rcornwell/sims i7010_cpu.c op_args[64]: M at 014 and D at 034 are both plain O_AB with no O_DBL.

upgraded.claim: Fact 11 (finder marked 'verified', independently re-confirmed here line by line): rcornwell/sims does not branch on instruction length in arithmetic execution; the one-field behaviour is produced entirely at fetch time by O_DBL.
upgraded.source: rcornwell/sims I7000/i7010_cpu.c: fetch loop `while(((br = FetchP(IAR)) & WM) == 0 && op_info != 0 && fault == 0)`; O_DBL applied only after a complete A address as `if (op_info & O_A) { AAR = STAR; if (op_info & O_DBL) { if (op_info & O_D) DAR = AAR; BAR = AAR; } }` (two sites, 1410 and 7010 address widths); execution `case OP_S: ValidAddr(AAR); ValidAddr(BAR); do_addsub(1);` / `case OP_A: ... do_addsub(0);` and OP_ZA/OP_ZS reading A at AAR and writing B at BAR with no length test. (https://github.com/rcornwell/sims/blob/master/I7000/i7010_cpu.c)

upgraded.claim: Fact 12 (re-confirmed verbatim against the file): cube1us/1410 note1410.txt entry 02379 'Add Instruction, chained' shows A field 10031 and B field 10034 — two distinct addresses; 02561 'Zero and Add Instruction, Chained from above' shows 'D: AAR=10231, BAR=10236'; 02544 annotates the genuine single-field ZA as 'A and B addresses have the same address.'

additions.claim: 1401-vs-1410, the single most important distinction the finding leaves open. The ANSWER for a 1-character chained op is the SAME on both machines — A24-1403-5 p.22: "All no-address instructions (Op code only) use the previous contents of the A- and B-address registers." But the SINGLE-ADDRESS rule is inverted. On the 1401, doubling is the DEFAULT: "Most single-address instructions (Op code and an A-address) cause the A-address to be inserted in both the A- and B-address registers (for example A xxx). However, MOVE, LOAD, and STORE A- or STORE B-ADDRESS REGISTER (Op codes M, L, Q, and H) do not disturb the [B-address register]." Confirmed at cycle level on p.20: "The B-address register is reset to blanks during the first part of the cycle for all operations except Move, Load, Store A- and Store B-address Register operation. During the I-1 cycle, the second instruction character (first character of the A-address) enters the thousands and hundreds positions of the A- and B-address registers." On the 1410 doubling is instead restricted to a named 'address double-type' group that EXCLUDES multiply (@) and divide (%). An emulator must therefore keep two separate tables: do NOT reuse the 1410 address-double set for 1401 compatibility mode, and specifically do not make 1401-mode @/% chain their B address the way 1410-mode @/% do.
additions.source: IBM A24-1403-5, IBM 1401 Data Processing System Reference Manual (Apr 1962), pp.20-22 (https://www.bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1401/A24-1403-5_1401_Reference_Apr62.pdf)

additions.claim: The 1401 single-address Add is semantically identical to the 1410 One Field Add, including the register contract — A24-1403-5 p.29: "This format of the ADD instruction causes the data in the A-field to be added to itself", Address Registers After Operation: I=NSI, A=A-LA, B=A-LA. Word marks: "The A-field must have a defining word mark. It is this word mark that stops the add operation." The 1401 also uses the identical LW symbol: "Lw — The number of characters in the A- or B-field, whichever is smaller" (p.22, Figure 18). So the FAMILY resemblance is real and the finding's 1410 reading is not 1401 contamination; only the mechanism that produces the doubling differs.
additions.source: IBM A24-1403-5, IBM 1401 Reference Manual, p.22 (Figure 18) and p.29 (https://www.bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1401/A24-1403-5_1401_Reference_Apr62.pdf)

additions.claim: The DAR mechanism the finding gestures at but never states cleanly. 223-2589 p.52: the A address is read into AAR and CAR for every not-percent-type op code, and additionally into BAR and DAR for address-double-type op codes; the B address is then read into BAR and DAR the same way. So DAR is a shadow of the B-field address, used at B-cycle units time ('DAR READ OUT CONTROL ARITHMETIC at B cycle, units control' — CE Handbook, Arithmetic-Type Op Codes). Every D cycle in the 1410 exists for exactly one purpose: to restore the invariant DAR == BAR when the instruction did not supply a B address. That is why a chained (I ring 1) arithmetic op takes one, why a 6-character NOT-address-double op (@ , %) takes one at I ring 6, and why a 6-character address-double op (A, S, ZA, ZS) takes none. An emulator that models only AAR/BAR can ignore D cycles entirely except for cycle counting.
additions.source: IBM 223-2589 1410 System Fundamentals p.52 (http://bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/223-2589_Instruction_Reference_1410_System_Fundamentals_Nov63.pdf); IBM 223-2588-2 1410 CE Handbook, 'Arithmetic-Type Op Codes (13.14.02)' and 'Add-Type Op Codes (13.14.02)' (https://bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/CE_Instruction_Reference_Maintenance/223-2588-2_1410_CE_Handbook_196404.pdf)

additions.claim: Open question #3 is answered: 1410 Autocoder DOES emit the 6-character one-address arithmetic form, and it is a first-class assembler mnemonic form, not a hand-deck-only curiosity. A22-0526-3's appendix 'Alphabetic Listing of Instructions in This Manual' lists both forms side by side under AUTOCODER / ACTUAL: "Add (One Field)  A a  ->  A (A)" versus "Add (Two Fields)  A a,b  ->  A (A) (B)"; likewise "Subtract (One Field) S a -> S (A)", "Zero and Add (One Field) ZA a", "Zero and Subtract (One Field) ZS a". So `A FIELDX` in Autocoder source assembles to a 6-character address-double add. The address-double path will be exercised by ordinary compiled programs, not only by diagnostics.
additions.source: IBM A22-0526-3 1410 Principles of Operation, Appendix, 'Alphabetic Listing of Instructions in This Manual (Indexed)' (http://bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/A22-0526-3_1410_princOps.pdf)

additions.claim: A decode invariant the finding misses that makes the whole ambiguity tractable in an emulator: 223-2589 p.13 — "The address of an instruction is the location of its operation code. No operation code has two valid lengths that differ by only one character. Instruction-length checking insures that the instruction length as read out of storage is one of the valid lengths for the particular operation code. The add op code, for example, has three valid lengths: 1, 6, or 11 characters." And A22-0526-3 p.11 'Instruction Length Validity' enumerates every legal word shape: O = 1, Od = 2, O xxx d = 5, O aaaaa = 6, O aaaaa d = 7, O xxx bbbbb d = 10, O aaaaa bbbbb = 11, O aaaaa bbbbb d = 12. There is exactly ONE Add op code with three lengths — not two op codes sharing a character — which is why 'one field' cannot be a separate decode.
additions.source: IBM 223-2589 1410 System Fundamentals p.13 (http://bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/223-2589_Instruction_Reference_1410_System_Fundamentals_Nov63.pdf); IBM A22-0526-3 1410 Principles of Operation p.11 (http://bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/A22-0526-3_1410_princOps.pdf)

additions.claim: Fact 13's list of d-character ops carrying the note "An instruction length of 6 chains the B-address and uses the last previous operation modifier" is incomplete: it appears on FIVE instructions in A22-0526-3, not four — Move Instructions (D, L = 1, 6 or 12), Table Lookup (T, L = 1, 6 or 12), Branch if Character Equal (B, L = 1, 6 or 12), Branch if Bit Equal (W, L = 1, 6 or 12), and Branch if Word Mark Present or Zone Equal (V, L = 1, 6 or 12). Table Lookup is missing from the finding. Note also that for BCE/BBE/BWZ the first address is an I-address (branch target), so their 6-character form is op + I-address with the B-address chained.
additions.source: IBM A22-0526-3 1410 Principles of Operation, 'Move Instructions', 'Table Lookup', 'Branch if Character Equal', 'Branch if Bit Equal', 'Branch if Word Mark Present, or Zone Equal' (http://bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/A22-0526-3_1410_princOps.pdf)

additions.claim: Independent numeric confirmation of the Two-Fields register contract from Jaeger's test deck that the finding did not extract: note1410.txt entry 02368 sets up A field at 10032 (1 character, value 1) and B field at 10036 (2 characters, value 05); the immediately following chained Add at 02379 runs with A field at 10031 and B field at 10034. 10032 - LW(=1) = 10031 and 10036 - LB(=2) = 10034 — exactly A-LW / B-LB. The ZA pair does the same: 02550 uses A at 10233 (2 chars) and B at 10239 (3 chars); the chained 02561 uses 10231 and 10236. This is a real hardware-derived check of the decrement rule, not just of the two-field reading.
additions.source: cube1us/1410, note1410.txt entries 02368/02379 and 02550/02561 (https://github.com/cube1us/1410), against A22-0526-3 Figure 8 p.12

additions.claim: The address-double family on the 1410 is broader than the six arithmetic ops, which matters if an emulator implements the flag generically. Clear Storage carries the same 'L = 1 or 6' one-address form (A22-1407-2: Clear Storage, T = 4.5(L + 1 + B), L = 1 or 6, registers NSI / B / xxx00-1) and is O_DBL in rcornwell/sims; so are Set Word Mark, Clear Word Mark, Branch, and the two I/O branch forms. The 1410 CE Handbook also puts Word Mark Op Codes in the group: 'Word Mark Op Codes (13.14.05) ... ADDRESS DOUBLE OP CODES if not 1401'.
additions.source: IBM A22-1407-2 1410 Reference Manual Nov61, Clear Storage (http://bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/A22-1407-2_1410ref_Nov61.pdf); IBM 223-2588-2 1410 CE Handbook, 'Word Mark Op Codes (13.14.05)' (https://bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/CE_Instruction_Reference_Maintenance/223-2588-2_1410_CE_Handbook_196404.pdf); rcornwell/sims i7010_cpu.c op_args[64]

additions.claim: The One-Field forms are not merely 'the two-field path with AAR==BAR' by assertion — the manuals' own termination rules confirm the two collapse. Two Fields (A22-0526-3 pp.17-18): "The B-field word mark stops the operation ... The A-field requires a word mark only if it is shorter than the B-field ... If the A-field is longer than the B-field, the high-order positions of the A-field that exceed the limit imposed by the B-field word mark are not processed." One Field (pp.17-19): "The A-field word mark stops the operation." With AAR == BAR the A-field word mark IS the B-field word mark, so the two rules are the same rule. rcornwell/sims' OP_ZA/OP_ZS path is also safe under aliasing: it reads the A character and captures the B word-mark bit before the first WriteP.
additions.source: IBM A22-0526-3 1410 Principles of Operation pp.17-19 (http://bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/A22-0526-3_1410_princOps.pdf); rcornwell/sims i7010_cpu.c OP_ZA/OP_ZS (https://github.com/rcornwell/sims/blob/master/I7000/i7010_cpu.c)

additions.claim: Op-code characters spot-checked against the manual's own instruction descriptions and index, no 1401 contamination found: A = Add (p.17), S = Subtract (p.17), ? = Zero and Add (p.18), ! = Zero and Subtract (p.18), @ = Multiply with Autocoder mnemonic M (p.19), % = Divide with Autocoder mnemonic D (p.20), D = Move, T = Table Lookup, B = Branch if Character Equal, W = Branch if Bit Equal, V = Branch if Word Mark or Zone Equal, C = Compare. The finding's table is correct on all of these. Note the deliberate near-collision an implementer can trip over: Autocoder mnemonic 'M' means Multiply but machine op-code character 'M' is a percent-type I/O op code, and Autocoder mnemonic 'D' means Divide but machine op-code character 'D' is Move.
additions.source: IBM A22-0526-3 1410 Principles of Operation, instruction descriptions pp.17-20 and the Appendix instruction index (http://bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/A22-0526-3_1410_princOps.pdf); percent-type op code list from IBM 223-2589 p.50 (http://bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/223-2589_Instruction_Reference_1410_System_Fundamentals_Nov63.pdf)

notes:
VERDICT: the finding's headline answer is CORRECT and I could not shake it. A 1-character chained A / S / ZA / ZS / @ / % on the IBM 1410 executes the two-field form, A at AAR and B at BAR. I re-read every load-bearing passage in primary sources rather than trusting the finder's quotations, and all four decisive quotations (A22-0526-3 p.12 chaining example; 223-2589 p.52 address-double read-out; 223-2589 p.52 chained-arithmetic D cycle; 223-2589 p.52 not-address-double B chaining) are verbatim accurate. Both behavioural oracles were re-read in full at the cited lines and both agree. The eight refutations above are corrections to mechanism detail, page citations and one piece of reasoning — none of them overturns the answer.

What changes for an emulator: (1) chained multiply/divide costs a D cycle AND a C cycle (E=2), not just a C cycle; (2) a 6-character multiply/divide costs a D cycle (E=1) while a 6-character add-type costs none (E=0); (3) CAR takes the A address for all not-percent-type ops, and DAR ends up holding the B address after any 11-character two-address instruction; (4) 1401 compatibility mode needs its own table — on the 1401 address doubling is the default for single-address instructions and is excluded only for M, L, Q, H, whereas on the 1410 it is an opt-in group that excludes @ and %.

On the 1401-vs-1410 hunt specifically: I found NO 1401 facts smuggled into the 1410 findings. The op codes, lengths, register symbols and termination rules all check out against A22-0526-3 and A22-1407-2. The one place the finding is exposed is the omitted 'if not 1401' qualifier on the ALD address-double lines, which I have corrected and then answered from the 1401 manual directly.

Method and limits. All 1410/1401 quotations were extracted with pdftotext -layout from bitsavers scans already staged locally in this session's scratchpad; I verified page attribution by walking to the nearest printed folio in the text layer. Page numbers I could NOT verify: the 223-2588-2 CE Handbook folios (the finding cites p.37 for the grouping chart and pp.40-41 for the grouping-line objectives) — the scan's text layer has no recoverable folios in that range, so I confirmed the CONTENT of every CE Handbook quotation verbatim but leave its page numbers unverified. Two of the finding's four open questions are now closed (#3 Autocoder emits the 6-character form; #4 partially — the 1401 rules are documented above and are NOT identical). Open question #1 (stale/invalid register after an intervening branch or I/O) remains genuinely undocumented beyond A22-0526-3 p.12's 'the address registers contain valid addresses' caution; I did not find any manual statement of behaviour, and note only that 223-2589 documents an address-validity check, not a defined result. Open question #2 (1410 CE Manual Oct61 data-flow charts) I also did not open, for the same reason the finder gave — 223-2589 p.52 plus the CE Handbook ALD objectives are already decisive and agree with each other.
